title: Reprice a two-helper basis change and nonsink terminal exchange on 679 owners
body:
Two literal nonsink exchanges preserve all 679 owners and full operators. One grade-two contact per call loses about 71.806626 signed units. Two contacts restore the new scratch in both orientations and double the loss.

## Scope and source

Uses the exact #7912 specialization. The 2,690 directional stock tests retain all existing packet values, main/411 owners and productive grade bins. The 3,552 inherited dirty retirements remain open. The source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`. The included source manifest identifies every public dependency used.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit679-nonsink-interface/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory, check its checksum manifest, and run the extracted commands. Cold replay reproduced both words, all 36 caller bindings, exact price and corrupted-owner and terminal controls. Hosted execution is separate.

## Open next questions

Change a pre-existing paid packet or productive target with a separately verified physical return.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. [Campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
